alternative: Freeze by default and copy explicitly at the write edge: frozen objects (including frozen_string_literal) plus Object#dup/String#+@ when a write is needed, new-object updates for value types, and Ractor.make_shareable when deep-frozen sharing across Ractors is the goal.
idiom_name: none - freeze plus dup/unary plus at the write boundary (no sharing test)
implementation_notes: Ruby offers no sharing count and no copy-before-mutation hook: Object#dup returns a shallow unfrozen copy, Object#clone keeps the singleton class and frozen state, and Object#freeze prevents modification rather than sharing it - so an implicitly shared body cannot be detected and transparent detach is off the table. The language-appropriate replacement is freeze-by-default with an explicit copy at the write edge: frozen string literals (the frozen_string_literal magic comment) are deduplicated by the runtime and unary plus produces a mutable copy only when the receiver is frozen, while Ractor.make_shareable deep-freezes an object graph so it can be shared without copying. Keep a hand-written handle/body only for a large buffer you own, tracking the sharing flag yourself.
code_sketch:
# frozen_string_literal: true

class Config
  attr_reader :hosts
  def initialize(hosts) = @hosts = hosts.freeze   # share a frozen list
  def with_host(h) = Config.new(@hosts + [h])     # write = copy + new value
end

Ractor.make_shareable(config)   # deep-freeze: shareable across Ractors
pitfalls: freeze is shallow: a frozen array of unfrozen strings is still unshareable (Ractor.shareable? reports false), so deep-freeze decisions must be made deliberately.
Object#dup is shallow and does not freeze: mutating a nested object through the copy is visible in the original.
Freezing an object that is already a Hash key or otherwise relied on for identity can raise FrozenError later - build the object completely before freezing.
Ractor.make_shareable deep-freezes the receiver in place and raises when a nested object cannot be frozen, so hand it a copy if the caller still needs a mutable version.
